title: Price tags for every context
summary: A price tag in TCG Card Shop Simulator is not one object: the game spawns it from a set of prefabs, so a shelf, an item box, a package box, a warehouse rack and a card each get the tag that fits them.
body: A price tag in this shop is not a single object that is copied everywhere. The game spawns tags from a set of prefabs, and which one appears depends on what is being tagged.
An ordinary tag is one of them. A shelf gets a group of world interface elements rather than a lone tag, which is why a whole bay can carry several prices that belong together.
Boxes have their own tags. There is a tag for an item box and a separate one for a package box, so a sealed box can show a price without pretending to be a loose item on a shelf.
The warehouse is covered too, with a tag for a warehouse rack, and cards have a tag of their own rather than sharing the one used for goods.

Prices are also shown when you check one. The panel that opens for a price carries the picture of the item, its name, the total and a line describing how the price has changed, so a decision can be made from the panel rather than by remembering what the number used to be.

That panel has separate arrows for the three outcomes: a price that has gone up, one that has gone down and one that has not changed. Keeping three markers rather than a signed number is how the game makes the direction readable at a glance.
The panel also has a card element and a prologue group of its own, so what you see when you check a card is not simply the same screen as when you check a tin.
What this entry does not tell you: what any of these tags looks like in detail, how a price change is worked out, or how often prices move. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Price tags are spawned from a set of prefabs rather than one tag being reused everywhere.
A shelf gets a group of world interface elements rather than a single tag.
There is a tag for an item box and a separate one for a package box.
There is a tag for a warehouse rack and a tag for a card.
The panel that shows a price carries the item image, its name, the total and a line for how the price has changed.

facts.claim: The panel has separate arrows for a price going up, going down and not changing.
The panel has a card element and a prologue group of its own.
The build ships item labels of its own, including a company label on the back.
